The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are consistent with this diagnosis, and the presence of these specific antibodies helps to distinguish it from other conditions such as Relapsing Polychondritis and Osteoarthritis.

The pericardial fluid cytology showing reactive mesothelial cells and lymphocytic infiltrate, as well as positive calretinin and CK5/6 staining, further supports this diagnosis.
